header.name: Introduction to Riemannian Geometry with Some Applications
header.description:
Riemannian Geometry evolved as a tool used by Relativity Theory, to understand the physics of the universe. More recently, it has found applications in fields such as Riemannian Computing in Computer Vision (RCCV), which has been defined as "the scientific area that integrates tools from Riemannian geometry and statistics to develop theoretical and computational solutions for optimization and statistical inference problems driven by applications in computer vision." (Riemannian Comuputing in Computer Vision, by P.K. Turaga and A. Srivastava, p. 1)

This course aims to equip students with some of the necessary mathematical tools needed to pursue further studies in these emerging fields.

We will begin the course with some preliminaries. We will cover some very basic topology, just enough to be able to define a manifold. We will also spend some time on differentiable manifolds, tangent spaces, and vector fields, before we introduce the concept of a Riemannian metric.

We will then study Riemannian manifolds, geodesics and the exponential map. Following this, the Grassmann manifold will be studied as a subtopic.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether a Riemannian structure can be applied in solving a problem.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to decide which Riemannian metric is most useful in studying a given problem.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to utilize the Riemannian metric, the exponential map, geodesics and other techniques in solving problems.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether geometric entity is a Grassmann manifold.
